title: Scalar-valued nonarchimedean Hahn–Banach over a field with compact closed balls
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$: $|a|=0$ if and only if $a=0$, $|1|=1$, and $|ab|=|a||b|$. Assume $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$ for all $a,b\in K$, some $t\in K$ satisfies $0<|t|<1$, and every closed ball $\{b\in K:|b-a|\leq r\}$ with $a\in K$ and $r\geq0$ is compact for the metric $d(a,b)=|a-b|$. Let $V$ be a $K$-vector space equipped with a norm $\|\cdot\|:V\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ satisfying $\|v\|=0$ if and only if $v=0$, $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$, and $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$, with the metric $d(v,w)=\|v-w\|$. For any $K$-linear subspace $W\subseteq V$ with the induced topology and any continuous $K$-linear map $f:W\to K$, there exists a continuous $K$-linear map $\widetilde f:V\to K$ such that $\widetilde f(w)=f(w)$ for every $w\in W$. Here linearity means additivity and preservation of scalar multiplication. No closedness of $W$ or completeness of $V$ is assumed.

proof.text: The ultrametric inequalities imply the ordinary triangle inequalities because $\max(r,s)\leq r+s$ for $r,s\geq0$. Thus $K$, $V$, and the induced norm on $W$ satisfy the normed-space hypotheses of [lem-trf-continuous-linear-map-norm-bound]. The given $t$ makes the scalar absolute value nontrivial. Apply that node with source $W$ and target $K$ to obtain one fixed real $C>0$ such that $|f(w)|\leq C\|w\|$ for all $w\in W$. We will extend $f$ while preserving this bound.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: obtain a uniform bound from continuity; Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.bound, Analysis/Normed/Operator/Basic.lean:132–133

proof.text:
Consider any subspace $U$ containing $W$ and linear extension $g:U\to K$ with $|g(u)|\leq C\|u\|$, and fix $x\in V\setminus U$. For each $u\in U$ put $R_u=C\|x-u\|$ and $B_u=\{b\in K:|b-g(u)|\leq R_u\}$. For $u,v\in U$,
$$|g(u)-g(v)|\leq C\|u-v\|\leq\max(R_u,R_v).$$
Consequently if $R_u\leq R_v$ and $b\in B_u$, the scalar ultrametric inequality gives $|b-g(v)|\leq\max(R_u,|g(u)-g(v)|)\leq R_v$. Hence $B_u\subseteq B_v$. In particular the balls are totally ordered by inclusion and each contains its center. Each ball is closed: for $y\notin B_u$ set $\epsilon=(|y-g(u)|-R_u)/2>0$. If $|z-y|<\epsilon$ and $z\in B_u$, the ordinary triangle inequality gives $|y-g(u)|\leq |y-z|+R_u<\epsilon+R_u<|y-g(u)|$, a contradiction.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: explicit center-distance, containment and closedness calculations for the admissible balls

proof.text: Use $B_0=\{b:|b|\leq C\|x\|\}$ as a topological space with its subspace topology. It is nonempty and compact by the hypothesis on $K$. The subsets $B_0\cap B_u$ are closed in $B_0$ by the preceding calculation. For a finite set $F\subseteq U$, select an index $u_*$ of least radius among $F\cup\{0\}$; a least member exists in this nonempty finite set of real radii. Then $B_{u_*}\subseteq B_0\cap\bigcap_{u\in F}B_u$, and its center belongs to that intersection. This also deals with $F=\varnothing$. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-closed-finite-intersection] to the compact space $B_0$ and the set-indexed closed family $(B_0\cap B_u)_{u\in U}$. Obtain $b\in\bigcap_{u\in U}B_u$. This is the compactness step (Stacks Tag 005D, lemma-intersection-closed-in-quasi-compact); no lower bound for the radii or completeness of $U$ is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: finite intersections inside the single compact ball B_0; Stacks Tag 005D

proof.text:
Every element of $U+Kx$ has a unique expression $u+ax$ with $u\in U$ and $a\in K$: two expressions with different coefficients would imply $x\in U$ by dividing their difference by the nonzero coefficient. Define $G(u+ax)=g(u)+ab$. This formula is additive and scalar-preserving by adding and scaling the unique expressions, and for $a=0$ it equals $g(u)$ and has the required bound. If $a\ne0$, put $v=-a^{-1}u\in U$. Since $b\in B_v$, linearity and norm homogeneity give
$$|G(u+ax)|=|a|\,|b-g(v)|\leq |a|C\|x-v\|=C\|u+ax\|.$$
Thus the explicitly constructed proper extension on $U+Kx$ preserves the same constant $C$. The uses of minus signs here follow from $|-1|=1$, which follows from multiplicativity and $(-1)^2=1$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: the linear formula and its bound on a one-vector enlargement

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S$ be the set of subsets of $V\times K$ that are graphs of linear maps $g:U\to K$, for subspaces $W\subseteq U\subseteq V$, restricting to $f$ on $W$ and satisfying $|g(u)|\leq C\|u\|$. This is a set, being a subfamily of the power set of $V\times K$, and it contains the graph of $f$. For a nonempty chain of such graphs, take their union. Comparability ensures a unique value at each vector in the union of the domains. Two vectors in that domain lie together in one chain member, so their sum and scalar multiples satisfy the same linear identities there. Thus the union is again the graph of a linear map on a subspace containing $W$; it agrees with $f$, and every value satisfies the same bound because it comes from one member. This union is an upper bound in $\mathcal S$. For the empty chain the graph of $f$ is an upper bound.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: check all chain-upper-bound hypotheses for the set of bounded partial-extension graphs

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zorn-lemma] with underlying set $V\times K$ and family $\mathcal S$, using the upper bounds just constructed, including the empty-chain case. Let the maximal graph be that of $g:U\to K$. If $U\ne V$, choose $x\in V\setminus U$ and repeat the ball construction and the explicit formula of steps 2–4 for this $U,g,x$. Step 3 uses [lem-sfb-compact-closed-finite-intersection] and supplies $b$; step 4 supplies a bounded extension to $U+Kx$. Its graph strictly contains the maximal graph, since its domain additionally contains $x$, a contradiction. Therefore $U=V$. Put $\widetilde f=g$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: Zorn maximality and contradiction by the one-vector construction

proof.text:
The maximal graph already ensures $K$-linearity and $\widetilde f|_W=f$. For every $v,w\in V$, linearity and its bound give
$$|\widetilde f(v)-\widetilde f(w)|\leq C\|v-w\|.$$
For any $\epsilon>0$, take $\delta=\epsilon/C>0$; then $\|v-w\|<\delta$ implies $|\widetilde f(v)-\widetilde f(w)|<\epsilon$. Hence $\widetilde f$ is continuous for exactly the prescribed metrics, proving every clause.
